title: Autoni hinattiin kolme kertaa
subtitle: My car was towed three times

blocks.text: Autoni has appeared unglossed since Lesson 2 — vein autoni, autoni hinattiin. And piti paikkansa, sitting quietly since Lesson 2 too, has been hiding a possessive suffix the whole time. Today both get explained: Finnish attaches 'my/his/her/their' directly onto the end of the noun, no separate word needed.

blocks.annotated: {Autoni|grammar|possessive suffix -ni|my car} {hinattiin|grammar|passive past|was towed} kolme kertaa.
blocks.translation: My car was towed three times.

blocks.title: One word instead of two
blocks.text: English needs two words: 'my' and 'car'. Formal written Finnish, the register of these reviews, often needs only one: autoni. In casual speech you'll sometimes hear the redundant-sounding mun autoni — the colloquial possessive word mun stacked in front of the suffix anyway — but the reviews here mostly use the clean, single-word version.

blocks.content: Add {-ni|grammar|possessive suffix|my} straight onto a noun to mean 'my [noun]'. Auto (car) → {autoni|grammar|possessive suffix -ni|my car}. No possessive pronoun word is needed at all — the suffix carries the whole meaning by itself.

items.en: I took my car to the repair shop.

blocks.title: The suffix you've been using since Lesson 2
blocks.text: Paikkansa, from piti paikkansa (Lesson 2, 'held true'), breaks down as paikka (place) + {-nsa|grammar|possessive suffix, 3rd person|its/his/her/their}. Literally: 'it held its own place'. Same job as -ni, just for 'its/his/her/their' instead of 'my'. You were already reading a possessive suffix two lessons before you had the word for it.

items.fi: He eivät kantaneet vastuuta {virheistään|grammar|possessive suffix, 3rd person, plural noun|their own mistakes}.
items.en: They didn't take responsibility for their own mistakes.

blocks.content: The same idea extends to 'we' and 'you (plural)': {-mme|grammar|possessive suffix|our} and {-nne|grammar|possessive suffix|your (pl.)}. Auto → automme, 'our car' — you already saw the shape meidän Focuksemme in Lesson 13's dialogue, which uses exactly this ending.

items.fi: {Automme|grammar|possessive suffix|our car} toimi hyvin huollon jälkeen.
items.en: Our car worked well after the service.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: My car was towed to the repair shop three times.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Did the price estimate hold true?

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: No. They didn't take responsibility for their own mistakes.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: Every possessive suffix does exactly the same job as the personal verb endings from Lesson 13 — -ni echoes -n (minä), -nsa echoes the hän pattern, -mme is identical in both systems. You're not learning six new rules; you're recognising one Finnish habit — marking 'whose' directly on the word — applied a second time.

blocks.content: Autoni: AU-to-ni (four even syllables, stress on AU). Paikkansa: PAIK-kan-sa (the double k is held, then a light final -sa). Virheistään: VIR-heis-tään (a mouthful — break it into vir-heis-tää-n and it settles down).

blocks.title: What you now own
items: the possessive suffix -ni — autoni, my car
-nsa/-nsä — the suffix hiding inside piti paikkansa since Lesson 2, now fully explained
-mme, -nne — our, your (plural), matching the verb endings from Lesson 13
you can now say 'my car', 'their mistake', 'our service' without a separate possessive word
you can look back at earlier lessons and recognise possessive suffixes you'd only half-noticed before
